question: How many nonprofits on the IRS 'safe to donate' list (Pub 78) also appear on the IRS auto-revocation list?
finding: 125,692 EINs sit on both the Pub 78 eligible-donee list and the IRS revocation list; 106,649 were formally reinstated, but 19,043 were revoked and never reinstated yet are still listed as eligible donees, with revocation years peaking in 2010 (2,821) and rising again 2020-2025 (~1,200-1,560/yr).
chart: plotly stacked bar: x=REV_YEAR, y=count, two series stacked = NEVER_REINSTATED_STILL_LISTED (emphasis color) and REINSTATED_STILL_LISTED (muted); companion choropleth/bar from by_state.csv on NEVER_REINSTATED_STILL_LISTED
caveats: Used ECONOMICS__FED_IRS_REVOCATION (1.19M rows, deduped, has WAS_REINSTATED) as the revocation list; FED_IRS_AUTO_REVOCATIONS (1.21M) is the same data with ~19k duplicate EINs. Neither is 500k-capped as previously suspected — both exceed 1.1M rows, and Pub 78 has 1.44M.
Reinstatement is judged only by the REINSTATEMENT_DATE/WAS_REINSTATED field in the revocation file; an org reinstated but not recorded there would be miscounted as 'never reinstated'.

Pub 78 and the revocation file are point-in-time snapshots that may have been pulled on different dates; some 'still listed' cases may be lag between IRS file updates, especially 2025-2026 revocations.
State comes from the revocation record's address, not Pub 78.
notable: 84.8% of the overlap is explained by legitimate reinstatements — the honest headline is the 19,043 unexplained ones.
2026 revocations already show 45 never-reinstated orgs still listed (fresh file lag, not scandal).
2010 spike is the first mass auto-revocation wave after the Pension Protection Act three-year non-filing rule kicked in.
